findings.title: Notes: no login
findings.detail: Anyone who can open the hub can read and change the notes, and notes can carry scripts (Space Lua, widgets) that run in each reader's browser (on the notes' own address, apart from /admin).
findings.fix: Choose who may open Notes (Apps): users with an account, or you alone; or leave it open if the notes are meant for everyone.

findings.title: The network floor
findings.detail: The hotspot is up and no floor is loaded: a guest on the hotspot reaches every listener on the box (SSH, Syncthing, MQTT, Tailscale, the rest).
findings.fix: Security → What a guest on the hotspot can reach: switch the floor on.

findings.detail: nginx keeps connections open (keepalive 8) and the hub drains request bodies.

steps.title: Unit sandboxing and the build unit

findings.title: Root units with a sandbox line missing
findings.detail: irate-box-ap-dns (missing ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, ProtectProc=invisible), irate-box-ap (missing ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, ProtectProc=invisible), irate-box-control (missing ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, ProtectProc=invisible), irate-box-crashwatch (missing ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, ProtectProc=invisible), irate-box-firewall (missing ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, ProtectProc=invisible), irate-box-secdoctor (missing ProtectProc=invisible), irate-box-tailscale-boot (missing ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, ProtectProc=invisible), irate-box-tailscale (missing ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, ProtectProc=invisible), irate-box-uplink (missing ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, ProtectProc=invisible), irate-box-visitors-switch (missing ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, ProtectProc=invisible), mosquitto (missing ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, ProtectProc=invisible), ttyd (missing ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, ProtectProc=invisible): a flaw in a root unit is root with nothing in between, and each line missing is one more thing the flaw can reach.
findings.fix: ProtectSystem=strict with real ReadWritePaths, NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, ProtectProc=invisible; narrow CapabilityBoundingSet and SystemCallFilter where possible.

findings.title: Guest-reachable units with a bare sandbox
findings.detail: irate-box-ci (keeps capabilities: cap_chown cap_dac_override cap_dac_read_search cap_fowner ca): guest-reachable services (the hub, fcgiwrap with cgit and git-http-backend, add-ons) with few of ProtectSystem=strict, NoNewPrivileges, PrivateTmp, ProtectHome, ProtectProc. The git servers run as the same user as the hub, with write access to the root helper's request queue.
findings.fix: Harden the units and give the git servers a user of their own.

findings.title: Builds can reach the hub on loopback (not /admin)
findings.detail: irate-box-ci.service can connect to 127.0.0.1, so builds reach the hub's guest API, as any guest can; /admin refuses them (it needs the front's secret, which builds cannot read).
findings.fix: IPAddressDeny=localhost on the unit, to keep builds off loopback altogether.

findings.detail: running, as hub; no problem found by the generic checks.

findings.fix: run it as an unprivileged or dynamic user

findings.title: Syncthing
findings.detail: running, as hub; no problem found by the generic checks or its own probe.

findings.title: MQTT broker for Meshtastic
findings.detail: running, as mosquitto. Port 1883 answers on *, 0.0.0.0, not only on loopback: anyone on the network reaches it directly, not through the front's login. Its install consent says: "The broker answers anyone on the box's network on port 1883, with no login (limited to msh/#). Add it?". Anonymous clients are allowed, limited by the ACL to msh/#.
findings.fix: bind to 127.0.0.1 and route it through the front, unless the network-facing port is the point; an access point's address only, and a password file, once the box is an AP

findings.title: Live collaboration (whiteboard)

findings.title: /proc visible to every user

findings.detail: claude-temp: owner ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL. A '-temp' file is a rule meant to be removed after the work it was added for.
findings.fix: Keep each only as long as it is needed: rm /etc/sudoers.d/<file>, then check `sudo -n true` fails.

findings.detail: None with a login shell.

steps.title: The hub's own accounts and sign-in

findings.title: Password hashes
findings.detail: Every account's hash is scrypt, at today's strength.

findings.title: Repository keys trusted for every repository
findings.detail: Keys in trusted.gpg.d (home_mPWRD_OS.gpg, network_Meshtastic_beta.gpg, network_Meshtastic_daily.gpg) can sign packages for any repository, Debian's included. Sources with no Signed-By of their own: home:mPWRD:OS.list: http://download.opensuse.org/repositories/home:/mPWRD:/OS/Debian_13/, network:Meshtastic:beta.list: http://download.opensuse.org/repositories/network:/Meshtastic:/beta/Debian_13/, network:Meshtastic:daily.list: http://download.opensuse.org/repositories/network:/Meshtastic:/daily/Debian_13/.
findings.fix: Move each key to /usr/share/keyrings and name it in its source's Signed-By (or [signed-by=…]); then the key vouches for that repository alone.

findings.title: A daily or nightly package channel
findings.detail: network:Meshtastic:daily.list: http://download.opensuse.org/repositories/network:/Meshtastic:/daily/Debian_13/ /: whatever its project built last lands on this box at the next upgrade, untested.
findings.fix: A release channel (stable or beta), unless the daily one is the point.

findings.title: A vendor kernel
findings.detail: 6.1.115-vendor-rockchip, built 2026-Jul-15: Debian's security tracker does not cover it, so debsecan's view of the box is blind to the kernel, and its fixes arrive only with a new image or kernel package from its maker.
findings.fix: Keep the kernel package current from its maker's repository when online (apt list --upgradable | grep linux-image).

findings.title: Bluetooth is on
findings.detail: bluetoothd runs, with a radio the hub does not use: a listener and a stack of its own, reachable by anyone in range.
findings.fix: systemctl disable --now bluetooth.service (and rtk-bluetooth.service where there is one); enable --now puts it back.

findings.title: Access-point profiles not the hub's
findings.detail: Hotspot (encrypted) in NetworkManager's connections: an access point the image set up, which could come up beside or instead of the hub's.
findings.fix: Delete each that is not yours (the hub's hotspot is not among them).

findings.title: Link protections
findings.detail: protected_symlinks and protected_hardlinks are on.
findings.fix: They only cover sticky world-writable folders: root's writes in hub-owned folders (F3) are not helped.

findings.detail: kptr_restrict=0, dmesg_restrict=0.
findings.fix: sysctl -w kernel.kptr_restrict=1 kernel.dmesg_restrict=1

steps.title: The CIS benchmark (debian-cis, in the deep audit)

findings.title: sudo's own log (CIS 1.3)
findings.detail: sudo can keep a log of every command run through it, apart from the journal. Not met here: logfile sudo. (deep audit of 2026-10-06 21:05)
findings.fix: Optional: the journal already records each use of sudo (with logs on the card, they survive a power cut).

findings.title: File integrity checking (Tripwire, AIDE) (CIS 1.4)
findings.detail: A tool that fingerprints the system's files and reports any change. Not met here: install tripwire, tripwire cron. (deep audit of 2026-10-06 21:05)
findings.fix: Heavy for a small board; the doctor's "Installed code" step already checks the hub's own files and their owners.

findings.title: Bootloader password (CIS 1.5)
findings.detail: The benchmark protects GRUB's menu with a password. Not met here: bootloader ownership, bootloader password. (deep audit of 2026-10-06 21:05)
findings.fix: This board boots with U-Boot, not GRUB; anyone holding the SD card owns the box regardless.

findings.title: Process hardening (NX, address randomisation, core dumps) (CIS 1.6)
findings.detail: Memory protections that make an exploit harder to aim, and no core dumps from privileged programs. Not met here: enable nx support, enable randomized vm placement, restrict core dumps. (deep audit of 2026-10-06 21:05)
findings.fix: Address randomisation and core dumps are kernel settings (sysctl); NX is the CPU's, reported oddly by the 32-bit ARM kernel.

findings.title: AppArmor (CIS 1.7)
findings.detail: Mandatory access control: profiles that confine what each program may touch. Not met here: install apparmor, enable apparmor, enforce or complain apparmor, enforcing apparmor. (deep audit of 2026-10-06 21:05)
findings.fix: The board's vendor kernel is built without AppArmor; the hub's units use systemd's sandboxing instead.

findings.title: Login banners (CIS 1.8)
findings.detail: A warning text shown before login (/etc/motd, /etc/issue). Not met here: motd perms. (deep audit of 2026-10-06 21:05)
findings.fix: Cosmetic; optional.

findings.title: Package updates (CIS 1.9)
findings.detail: Updates waiting to be installed. Not met here: install updates. (deep audit of 2026-10-06 21:05)
findings.fix: See Debian's security updates (Updates).

findings.title: Time synchronisation (CIS 2.2)
findings.detail: A time service (systemd-timesyncd or chrony) keeping the clock right. Not met here: configure systemd-timesyncd, configure ntp. (deep audit of 2026-10-06 21:05)
findings.fix: The box keeps its own time (the Clock pane): with no internet there is nothing to synchronise with.

findings.title: IPv6 (CIS 3.1)
findings.detail: The benchmark turns IPv6 off where it is not used. Not met here: disable ipv6. (deep audit of 2026-10-06 21:05)
findings.fix: Your network may use it; the doctor's "Reached from the internet" step checks what IPv6 exposes.

findings.title: Sending ICMP redirects (CIS 3.2)
findings.detail: A host that is not a router should not tell others how to route. Not met here: disable send packet redirects. (deep audit of 2026-10-06 21:05)
findings.fix: sysctl net.ipv4.conf.all.send_redirects=0 (and .default): safe on the box, guests' internet included.

findings.title: Network parameters (source routing, redirects, martians, router adverts) (CIS 3.3)
findings.detail: Kernel network settings that refuse forged routes and log impossible addresses. Not met here: disable source routed packets, disable icmp redirect, disable secure icmp redirect, log martian packets, enable source route validation, disable ipv6 router advertisement. (deep audit of 2026-10-06 21:05)
findings.fix: Mostly safe to set by sysctl; leave accept_ra on if your network gives IPv6 addresses by router adverts.

findings.title: Auditing (auditd) (CIS 4.1)
findings.detail: The kernel's audit system, recording security events in detail. Not met here: install auditd, enable auditd, audit bootloader, audit backlog limit, audit log storage, halt when audit log full, keep all audit logs, record date time edit, record user group edit, record network edit…. (deep audit of 2026-10-06 21:05)
findings.fix: The vendor kernel is built without CONFIG_AUDIT, so auditd cannot run on this board.

findings.title: Logging (syslog-ng, a persistent journal) (CIS 4.2)
findings.detail: Logs kept on disk, with tight permissions, and sent to another machine. Not met here: install syslog-ng, enable syslog-ng, syslog ng logfiles perm, syslog-ng remote host, remote syslog-ng acl, journald write persistent, logs permissions. (deep audit of 2026-10-06 21:05)
findings.fix: Keep logs on the card (Security) covers what matters here; a remote log server needs a second machine.

findings.title: logrotate's permissions (CIS 4.4)
findings.detail: Rotated logs created readable by root only. Not met here: logrotate permissions. (deep audit of 2026-10-06 21:05)
findings.fix: By hand: create 0640 in /etc/logrotate.conf.

findings.title: cron's files' permissions (CIS 5.1)
findings.detail: /etc/crontab and /etc/cron.* readable by root only. Not met here: crontab perm ownership, cron hourly perm ownership, cron daily perm ownership, cron weekly perm ownership, cron monthly perm ownership, cron d perm ownership, cron users. (deep audit of 2026-10-06 21:05)
findings.fix: By hand: sudo chmod og-rwx /etc/crontab /etc/cron.hourly /etc/cron.daily /etc/cron.weekly /etc/cron.monthly /etc/cron.d

findings.title: SSH server settings (CIS 5.2)
findings.detail: sshd's settings: who may log in, how, for how long, with which ciphers. Not met here: sshd conf perm ownership, sshd protocol, sshd loglevel, disable x11 forwarding, sshd maxauthtries, enable sshd ignorerhosts, disable sshd hostbasedauthentication, disable root login, disable sshd permitemptypasswords, disable sshd setenv…. (deep audit of 2026-10-06 21:05)
findings.fix: The ones that matter (root login, passwords, forwarding) are choices on Security; the rest are fine-tuning in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d.

findings.title: Password quality and lockout (PAM) (CIS 5.3)
findings.detail: Rules for strong passwords and locking an account after failed tries. Not met here: enable pwquality, enable lockout failed password, limit password reuse. (deep audit of 2026-10-06 21:05)
findings.fix: They matter only where a password logs in: with SSH on keys only, that is the console.

findings.title: Password ageing, umask, shell timeout (CIS 5.4)
findings.detail: Passwords that expire, new files private by default, idle shells logged out. Not met here: set password exp days, set password min days change, default umask, default timeout. (deep audit of 2026-10-06 21:05)
findings.fix: Optional on a single-owner box; expiring passwords mostly make people write them down.

findings.title: Who may use su (CIS 5.6)
findings.detail: su limited to the members of one group. Not met here: restrict su. (deep audit of 2026-10-06 21:05)
findings.fix: Optional: root's password is locked, so su leads nowhere anyway.

findings.title: World-writable, unowned and setuid files (CIS 6.1)
findings.detail: Files anyone may change, files with no owner, and programs that run as root. Not met here: find world writable file, find unowned files, find ungrouped files, find suid files. (deep audit of 2026-10-06 21:05)
findings.fix: Look at the list from a shell: sudo find / -xdev \( -perm -0002 -type f -o -nouser -o -nogroup \) -ls

findings.title: Users' own files' permissions (CIS 6.2)
findings.detail: Dot files in home folders writable by others. Not met here: check user dot file perm. (deep audit of 2026-10-06 21:05)
findings.fix: By hand: chmod go-w on each file named.

findings.title: USB devices (CIS 99.1)
findings.detail: The benchmark blocks USB storage. Not met here: disable usb devices, acc sudoers no all. (deep audit of 2026-10-06 21:05)
findings.fix: The box reads books and updates from USB sticks on purpose.

findings.title: TCP wrappers (hosts.deny) (CIS 99.3)
findings.detail: An old access list for network services. Not met here: install tcp wrapper, hosts deny. (deep audit of 2026-10-06 21:05)
findings.fix: Debian 13's sshd no longer reads it; the floor (Security) is what filters the hotspot.

findings.title: Kernel audit support (CIS 99.4)
findings.detail: CONFIG_AUDIT in the kernel, for auditd. Not met here: enable auditd kernel. (deep audit of 2026-10-06 21:05)
findings.fix: The vendor kernel is built without it.

findings.title: More SSH settings (CIS 99.5)
findings.detail: Further sshd hardening: keys only, rekeying, strict modes, where keys may come from. Not met here: ssh auth pubk only, ssh cry rekey, ssh disable features, ssh keys from, ssh strict modes. (deep audit of 2026-10-06 21:05)
findings.fix: Keys only is a choice on Security; the rest are fine-tuning in /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d.

findings.title: Logs live in RAM
findings.detail: /var/log is a RAM disk (Armbian's ramlog): sshd's log and the journal are trimmed every 15 minutes and gone at a power cut, so the evidence of an intrusion goes with them; the doctor's "reached from the internet" sees only since the last boot. (scan of 2026-10-09 02:39)
findings.fix: Logs on the card, a few MB a week: Armbian's ramlog off and the journal kept, capped at 32 MB. It applies from the next boot.

findings.title: What a guest on the hotspot can reach
findings.detail: Everything that listens on the box, SSH and the rest: there is no floor. The floor would allow, on ap0 alone: TCP 53, 80, 443, 1883, 8090, 8091, 8092, 8093, 8490, 8491, 8492, 8493, 22000; UDP 53, 67, 21027, 22000; and drop the rest. The box's other networks are not touched. (scan of 2026-10-09 02:39)
findings.fix: A default-drop ruleset on the hotspot's interface, loaded at boot, at one of two levels: the hub and its apps, or the hub alone (its apps' ports closed to guests). MQTT and Syncthing open to guests where installed, SSH only if you say so. Undo here.
